report.headline: SA1 five-minute RRP peak 4981.0 $/MWh at 2026-07-31 02:05 ACST (UTC+0930)
summary: A single prolonged high-price episode in SA1 peaked at 4981.0 $/MWh (interval ending 2026-07-31 02:05 ACST (UTC+0930)).
There were 214 five-minute intervals at-or-above the analysis threshold of 300.0 $/MWh in the window.
The dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the five-minute price peak was 1472.82 MW (dispatch TOTALDEMAND measure).
Net interchange at the five-minute price peak was -82.59 MW (net flow into SA1).
The half-hour operational demand in the half-hour containing the price extreme (interval ending 2026-07-30 17:00:00 UTC) was 1466.0 MW.
The window maximum half-hour operational demand was 2173.0 MW.
SCADA-observed unit changes in the 2026-07-30T15:00:00Z–2026-07-30T18:00:00Z window include BLYTHB −59.57 MW, BARKIPS −45.81 MW, AGLHAL −38.97 MW and PAREP +11.51 MW (descriptive SCADA observations).

AEMO published a market notice reporting a 'Non-credible contingency event - SA region - 30/07/2026' that states "At 1140 hrs, the City West 275/66 kV transformer T_1 and the 275 kV circuit breaker 6675 tripped during restoration of City West 275/66 kV transformer T_2." [c1]

possible_explanations.statement: Local generator output reductions observed in SCADA (examples: BLYTHB, BARKIPS, AGLHAL) might have contributed to supply tightness around the price spike; see SCADA observations and unit-change evidence (these are descriptive SCADA observations only).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain unit outage declarations, unit availability reports and rebid logs for the named units for 2026-07-30 to determine whether the SCADA reductions reflect outages, ramping, or rebids.

possible_explanations.statement: A reduction in available imports or a change in interconnector capability might have coincided with the spike; net interchange at the peak was −82.59 MW (net flow into SA1).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Retrieve interconnector availability records, constraint change notices and pre-dispatch/interconnector limit data around the peak to see whether import capability was restricted.

possible_explanations.statement: The AEMO market notice describing a 'Non-credible contingency event' earlier on 30/07/2026 might be related to system conditions that day [c1] and could plausibly have affected operations later, but the notice text does not link that event to the price spike.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare the transformer trip notice [c1] timeline and any subsequent dispatch constraint or outage bulletins; check post-event dispatch notes and constraint changes to see if operational limits persisted into the price spike period.

possible_explanations.statement: Demand levels around the peak (the half-hour containing the price extreme was 1466.0 MW and the window maximum half-hour operational demand was 2173.0 MW) might have interacted with available supply and interchange to produce the observed prices.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare pre-dispatch forecasts versus actual demand, and inspect offer stacks and rebids in the hours before the spike to see how supply availability matched demand.

uncertainties: SCADA generation changes are descriptive observations and do not by themselves identify whether a unit was unavailable, tripped, or was rebid.
The retrieved market notice [c1] reports a transformer/breaker trip but does not state operational impacts that would directly link it to the 16:35 UTC price peak.

Rebid logs and offer stack data for SA1 covering 2026-07-30 15:00:00Z–18:00:00Z.
Interconnector availability records and constraint change notices for the interconnectors serving SA1 around the peak.
